question: What is the most common developmental complication in bacterial meningitis in the pediatric age?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Bacterial meningitis -> inflammation of the meninges -> increased intracranial pressure -> hydrocephalus -> 80% CHAIN: Bacterial meningitis -> inflammatory response -> damage to the auditory nerve -> hearing loss -> 70% CHAIN: Bacterial meningitis -> brain damage -> cognitive impairment -> mental retardation -> 60% CHAIN: Bacterial meningitis -> inflammation of the optic nerve -> visual defects -> 50% CHAIN: Bacterial meningitis -> disruption of brain activity -> increased risk of seizures -> residual epilepsy -> 80%
analysis: Bacterial meningitis in the pediatric age can lead to various complications, but the most common developmental complication is typically hearing loss.
